fields.question_text: 1. What is the time complexity to access an element at index i in a standard static array of size N?
fields.explanation: Arrays store elements in contiguous memory. Address is computed in O(1) time using BaseAddress + i * ElementSize.

fields.question_text: 2. What is the worst-case time complexity of inserting an element at the beginning (index 0) of an array of size N?
fields.explanation: All N existing elements must be shifted right by one position, requiring O(N) operations.

fields.question_text: 3. In dynamic arrays (e.g. C++ vector, Python list), what is the amortized time complexity of appending an element to the end?
fields.explanation: Although resizing requires doubling capacity (O(N)), it occurs infrequently. The overall cost averaged over N appends is O(1) amortized.

fields.question_text: 4. Which property of arrays makes them extremely efficient for CPU execution compared to linked lists?
fields.explanation: Contiguous memory layout maximizes CPU L1/L2 cache line prefetches, minimizing cache misses.

fields.question_text: 5. Given a 2D array of dimensions R x C stored in row-major order, what is the formula for the offset of element at row i, col j?
fields.explanation: In row-major ordering, row i skips i full rows of size C, so offset = i * C + j.

fields.question_text: 6. What technique computes the sum of any contiguous subarray [L, R] in O(1) time after O(N) preprocessing?
fields.explanation: Sum(L, R) = Prefix[R] - Prefix[L-1]. After precomputing prefix sums in O(N), queries run in O(1).

fields.question_text: 7. In a sorted array of N distinct elements, what is the maximum number of comparisons needed to search for a key using Binary Search?
fields.explanation: Binary search halves the search space each step, yielding floor(log2 N) + 1 maximum comparisons.

fields.question_text: 8. Which algorithm finds the maximum subarray sum in linear O(N) time?
fields.explanation: Kadane's algorithm maintains running max_ending_here = max(arr[i], max_ending_here + arr[i]) in O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 9. What is the space complexity of reversing an array in-place using two pointers?
fields.explanation: Swapping elements at left and right pointers inward modifies the existing array using O(1) extra space.

fields.question_text: 10. In the 'Dutch National Flag' algorithm (sorting 0s, 1s, 2s), how many pointers are maintained?
fields.explanation: It maintains low, mid, and high pointers to partition elements into 0s, 1s, and 2s in a single O(N) pass.

fields.question_text: 11. If an array of size N contains numbers from 1 to N with one missing number, how can you find it in O(N) time and O(1) space?
fields.option_b: Sum formula N*(N+1)/2 minus actual sum
fields.explanation: The sum of 1 to N is N*(N+1)/2. Subtracting the actual array sum yields the missing number in O(N) time & O(1) space.

fields.question_text: 12. What is the worst-case space complexity of storing a sparse matrix using a standard 2D array of size M x N?
fields.explanation: A standard 2D array allocates memory for all M*N entries, even if most elements are zero.

fields.question_text: 13. In the 2Sum problem (find 2 elements in sorted array summing to Target), what is the optimal time & space complexity using Two Pointers?
fields.option_b: O(N log N) time, O(N) space
fields.explanation: With left=0 and right=N-1 pointers on a sorted array, moving inward takes O(N) time and O(1) extra space.

fields.question_text: 14. How can you rotate an array of N elements to the right by K steps in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space?
fields.option_a: Reverse full array, then reverse first K elements, then reverse remaining N-K elements
fields.explanation: 3-step array reversal rotates in-place in linear O(N) time and constant O(1) space.

fields.question_text: 15. What is the worst-case time complexity of Majority Element algorithm (Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm)?
fields.explanation: Boyer-Moore Voting algorithm finds candidate majority element in 1 pass O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

fields.question_text: 16. In 2D Matrix binary search on a sorted matrix of size M x N where matrix[i][j] < matrix[i][j+1] and matrix[i][C-1] < matrix[i+1][0], how is 1D index mid mapped to (row, col)?
fields.option_a: row = mid // N, col = mid % N
fields.option_b: row = mid % M, col = mid // M
fields.option_c: row = mid // M, col = mid % M
fields.option_d: row = mid * N, col = mid + N
fields.explanation: Virtual 1D array of length M*N maps index to 2D coordinates via row = mid // N and col = mid % N.

fields.question_text: 17. What is the time complexity to find the median of two sorted arrays of sizes M and N using binary search on partitions?
fields.explanation: Binary search on partition point of smaller array runs in logarithmic O(log(min(M, N))) time.

fields.question_text: 18. What is the maximum number of contiguous subarrays in an array of size N?
fields.explanation: Choosing start L and end R indices yields N + (N-1) + ... + 1 = N*(N+1)/2 contiguous subarrays.

fields.question_text: 19. Which array operation requires O(N) time even in a sorted array?
fields.option_c: Inserting a new element while preserving sorted order
fields.explanation: Inserting into a sorted array requires shifting elements to make room, taking O(N) worst-case time.

fields.question_text: 20. In Trapping Rain Water problem, what is the optimal time and space complexity using two pointers?
fields.option_c: O(N log N) time, O(1) space
fields.explanation: Two pointers maintaining left_max and right_max calculate trapped water in a single linear pass.

fields.question_text: 21. What does Product of Array Except Self problem require to achieve O(N) time without using division operation?
fields.option_b: Prefix products and Suffix products accumulation
fields.explanation: Accumulating prefix products in one pass and suffix products in reverse pass yields answer in O(N) without division.

fields.question_text: 22. In Next Permutation algorithm, what is the first step to find lexicographically next greater permutation of an array?
fields.option_b: Find first decreasing element arr[i] from right where arr[i] < arr[i+1]
fields.explanation: Scan from right to find pivot arr[i] < arr[i+1], then swap with next larger element on right and reverse suffix.

fields.question_text: 23. In an array of size N, what is the total number of non-empty subsequences?
fields.explanation: Each element can either be included or excluded (2^N combinations), excluding empty set gives 2^N - 1.

fields.question_text: 24. What is the time complexity of 3Sum problem using sorting and two pointers?
fields.explanation: Sorting takes O(N log N). Fixing 1 outer element and running 2 pointers inward takes O(N) per outer element, giving O(N^2) total.

fields.question_text: 25. In monotonic array checking, what is the best time complexity to determine if an array is strictly increasing or decreasing?
fields.explanation: A single linear pass scanning adjacent elements arr[i] vs arr[i+1] checks monotonicity in O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 1. What is the time complexity of checking if two strings of length N are anagrams using character frequency arrays?
fields.explanation: Increment frequencies for string 1 and decrement for string 2 in a single pass of size N (O(N) time, O(1) char space).

fields.question_text: 2. In Java / Python, strings are immutable. What does string concatenation s += 'a' inside a loop of size N cost overall in time?
fields.explanation: Creating a new string buffer of length i at iteration i results in sum(1..N) = O(N^2) total work.

fields.question_text: 3. What auxiliary structure is recommended to perform efficient repeated string concatenations in Java/Python?
fields.explanation: StringBuilder or list of characters appends in amortized O(1) time per operation, achieving total linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 4. What is the worst-case time complexity of Brute Force pattern matching of pattern P (len M) in text T (len N)?
fields.explanation: At each of the N positions in text, comparing M characters takes O(M) operations in worst case (e.g. T='AAAAA', P='AAB').

fields.question_text: 5. What array precomputed by KMP algorithm allows skipping unnecessary re-comparisons during pattern search?
fields.explanation: LPS array stores the length of the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix, enabling O(N + M) KMP matching.

fields.question_text: 6. What is the time complexity to construct the LPS array in KMP algorithm for pattern of length M?
fields.explanation: Preprocessing the LPS array takes linear O(M) time by maintaining a matching prefix pointer.

fields.question_text: 7. What hashing technique does Rabin-Karp algorithm use to update substring hash in O(1) time while sliding a window across text?
fields.explanation: Rolling hash subtracts leaving char * p^(M-1) and adds entering char in O(1) time per window slide.

fields.question_text: 8. What algorithm finds the longest palindromic substring in strictly linear O(N) time?
fields.explanation: Manacher's algorithm utilizes mirror symmetry across palindrome centers to compute all palindrome radii in O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 9. In Manacher's algorithm, why are special separator characters (like '#') inserted between string characters?
fields.option_b: To treat even-length and odd-length palindromes uniformly
fields.explanation: Transforming 'aba' to '#a#b#a#' ensures all palindromes become odd length around a single center node.

fields.question_text: 10. What does Z[i] represent in the Z-Algorithm for string processing?
fields.option_a: Length of longest substring starting at index i matching prefix of string S
fields.explanation: Z-array entry Z[i] stores the length of the longest common prefix between S and the suffix of S starting at i.

fields.question_text: 11. What is the overall time complexity of Z-Algorithm to build Z-array for string of length N?
fields.explanation: Z-algorithm maintains rightmost matching window boundary [L, R], achieving linear O(N) computation.

fields.question_text: 12. In Minimum Window Substring problem (find min window in S containing all chars of T), what algorithm pattern is optimal?
fields.option_b: Sliding Window with Character Frequency Map
fields.explanation: Expanding right pointer and shrinking left pointer while tracking required character frequencies runs in O(|S| + |T|) time.

fields.question_text: 13. What is the time complexity of reversing words in a string of length N in-place?
fields.explanation: Reversing full string then reversing individual words in-place takes two passes of linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 14. How many distinct non-empty substrings can be formed from a string of length N with distinct characters?
fields.explanation: Substrings are contiguous. Selecting start and end positions yields N*(N+1)/2 distinct substrings.

fields.question_text: 15. In Longest Common Prefix problem among array of K strings of max length L, what is the worst-case time complexity using horizontal scanning?
fields.explanation: Comparing strings sequentially scans up to L characters across K strings, taking O(K * L) operations.

fields.question_text: 16. In Run-Length Encoding (compression), string 'AAABBC' compresses to:
fields.explanation: Consecutive repeated characters are replaced by character followed by count: A3B2C1 (or A3B2C).

fields.question_text: 17. What is the time complexity of checking if string S is a rotation of string T of length N?
fields.option_b: Check if length matches AND T is substring of S+S in O(N) time
fields.explanation: S+S contains all possible rotations of S. Checking if T is substring of S+S takes linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 18. What data structure allows finding all matching occurrences of K patterns in text T (len N) simultaneously in O(N + total_matches) time?
fields.explanation: Aho-Corasick builds failure links on a Trie of patterns, processing text in single O(N) linear sweep.

fields.question_text: 19. In Suffix Automaton, what is the maximum number of states for a string of length N > 2?
fields.explanation: Suffix Automaton is a highly compact representation of all substrings of S with at most 2N-1 states and 3N-4 transitions.

fields.question_text: 20. What is the space complexity to store a Trie containing N words of average length L with lowercase English alphabet?
fields.explanation: Each Trie node contains an array of size 26 (alphabet size). Total nodes bounded by N * L, giving O(N * L * 26).

fields.question_text: 21. What is the main cause of Hash Collisions in Rabin-Karp algorithm?
fields.option_b: Two different substrings producing identical numerical hash modulo M
fields.explanation: Because infinite strings map to finite hash values under modulo M, different strings can produce equal hash values.

fields.question_text: 22. In Isomorphic Strings problem ('egg' and 'add'), two strings are isomorphic if:
fields.option_b: Characters in S can be replaced to get T with a 1-to-1 unique mapping
fields.option_c: They are reverse of each other
fields.explanation: Every character in S must map uniquely to a character in T with no two characters mapping to same target.

fields.question_text: 23. In Edit Distance (Levenshtein Distance) between string S (len M) and T (len N), what operations are allowed?
fields.explanation: Standard Levenshtein edit distance computes minimum insertions, deletions, or substitutions to transform S to T.

fields.question_text: 24. What is the time complexity of computing Edit Distance using 2D Dynamic Programming matrix?
fields.explanation: DP matrix of size (M+1) x (N+1) fills each state in O(1) time, yielding O(M * N) time.

fields.question_text: 25. Which string comparison algorithm is invariant to case sensitivity and extra whitespace when parsing tokens?
fields.explanation: Trimming whitespace and lowercasing strings before tokenization standardizes comparisons across variations.

fields.question_text: 1. What does a pointer variable store in C / C++?
fields.explanation: A pointer variable stores the memory address location where another variable resides.

fields.question_text: 2. Given int *ptr and sizeof(int) = 4, if ptr holds address 0x1000, what is the value of (ptr + 2)?
fields.explanation: Pointer arithmetic scales addition by target type size: 0x1000 + 2 * sizeof(int) = 0x1000 + 8 = 0x1008.

fields.question_text: 3. What does dereferencing a pointer (*ptr) perform?
fields.option_b: Accesses the actual value stored at the address ptr points to
fields.explanation: The dereference operator '*' accesses or modifies the value located at the address held in ptr.

fields.question_text: 4. What is a 'Dangling Pointer'?
fields.option_b: A pointer referencing a memory location that has been deallocated/freed
fields.option_c: A pointer pointing to constant string
fields.explanation: Dangling pointers point to memory that was freed or went out of scope, causing undefined behavior on dereference.

fields.question_text: 5. What is a 'Null Pointer'?
fields.option_a: Pointer holding address 0 (nullptr) indicating it points to no valid memory
fields.explanation: NULL / nullptr signifies an unassigned pointer pointing to no valid memory object.

fields.question_text: 6. What operator is used to get the memory address of an existing variable in C/C++?
fields.explanation: The address-of operator '&' returns the memory address location of a variable.

fields.question_text: 7. What is a 'Memory Leak' in C / C++?
fields.option_b: Dynamically allocated heap memory (malloc/new) that is no longer accessible and never freed
fields.explanation: Failing to free dynamically allocated heap memory prevents memory reuse, leading to leaks.

fields.question_text: 8. What does double pointer int **ptr store?
fields.option_b: Address of another pointer variable (pointer to pointer)
fields.explanation: int **ptr stores the memory address of a pointer variable that points to an int.

fields.question_text: 9. In C, what function allocates requested bytes of uninitialized heap memory and returns a void pointer?
fields.explanation: malloc(size) allocates requested bytes on heap without initializing memory contents.

fields.question_text: 10. How does calloc(n, size) differ from malloc(n * size)?
fields.option_b: calloc initializes allocated memory bytes to zero
fields.explanation: calloc initializes all allocated bytes to zero; malloc leaves memory filled with garbage values.

fields.question_text: 11. What operator replaces (*ptr).member in C/C++ for structure pointers?
fields.explanation: The arrow operator ptr->member is syntactic shortcut for dereferencing and accessing structure member (*ptr).member.

fields.question_text: 12. What happens when you attempt to dereference a NULL pointer (*nullptr)?
fields.explanation: Dereferencing NULL triggers access violation causing Segmentation Fault.

fields.question_text: 13. What is the size of a pointer variable (e.g. char*, int*, double*) on a 64-bit operating system architecture?
fields.explanation: On 64-bit systems, all pointers require 64 bits (8 bytes) to store memory addresses, regardless of target type.

fields.question_text: 14. What is a 'Wild Pointer'?
fields.option_b: An uninitialized pointer storing random garbage memory address
fields.explanation: Uninitialized pointers hold arbitrary memory addresses; dereferencing them is dangerous.

fields.question_text: 15. How can you pass a pointer by reference to a function in C to modify the original pointer itself?
fields.explanation: Passing double pointer int **ptr allows modifying the original pointer address inside caller scope.

fields.question_text: 16. In C++, what smart pointer type manages exclusive ownership of dynamic heap memory and prevents copy assignment?
fields.explanation: std::unique_ptr owns heap object exclusively and deallocates automatically when going out of scope.

fields.question_text: 17. What smart pointer maintains a reference count of owners sharing heap memory in C++?
fields.explanation: std::shared_ptr uses reference counter, deleting managed object when count reaches zero.

fields.question_text: 18. What issue occurs when two std::shared_ptr instances reference each other cyclically?
fields.option_b: Cyclic Reference Memory Leak (Reference count never hits 0)
fields.explanation: Cyclic references prevent reference count from reaching 0, causing memory leak. std::weak_ptr breaks cycles.

fields.question_text: 19. In array decay: when array name 'arr' is passed to a function void foo(int arr[]), what does 'arr' decay into inside foo?
fields.option_b: Pointer to first element int* arr
fields.explanation: Arrays decay to pointer to first element when passed as function parameters, losing sizeof array length.

fields.question_text: 20. What is a 'Void Pointer' (void*) in C/C++?
fields.option_b: Generic pointer that can hold address of any data type without type information
fields.explanation: void* is a generic raw address pointer; it must be type-cast before dereferencing.

fields.question_text: 21. What is the result of subtracting two pointers pointing to elements in the same array: (ptr2 - ptr1)?
fields.option_b: Number of elements between ptr1 and ptr2 (ptrdiff_t)
fields.explanation: Subtracting two pointers of same type returns the count of elements between them.

fields.question_text: 22. What does function pointer syntax int (*func_ptr)(int, int) declare?
fields.option_b: Pointer variable func_ptr to a function taking two ints and returning int
fields.explanation: int (*func_ptr)(int, int) declares pointer holding executable code address of function with matching signature.

fields.question_text: 23. In C++, what operator is used to allocate memory on heap and invoke constructor?
fields.explanation: new operator allocates heap space and calls constructor; delete calls destructor and frees heap.

fields.question_text: 24. What happens when calling free(ptr) on a memory pointer that was ALREADY freed?
fields.option_b: Double Free Vulnerability / Undefined Behavior crash
fields.explanation: Double freeing heap memory corrupts heap metadata allocator state, leading to crashes or security flaws.

fields.question_text: 25. Which memory area stores local function variables, parameter pointers, and return addresses?
fields.explanation: Stack memory manages local stack frames, automatically allocating on function entry and freeing on exit.

fields.question_text: 1. What mandatory component must every recursive function possess to prevent infinite execution?
fields.explanation: The base case provides termination conditions where the function returns without making further recursive calls.

fields.question_text: 2. What error occurs when a recursive function lacks a valid base case or recurses too deeply?
fields.explanation: Each recursive call consumes a call stack frame; exceeding stack limit causes Stack Overflow.

fields.question_text: 3. What is 'Tail Recursion'?
fields.option_b: Recursive call is the absolute final action performed in the function
fields.explanation: In tail recursion, no operations remain after the recursive call, allowing compilers to reuse stack frames.

fields.question_text: 4. Why is Tail Call Optimization (TCO) beneficial?
fields.option_b: Reuses current stack frame, reducing auxiliary stack space from O(N) to O(1)
fields.explanation: TCO converts tail-recursive functions into iterative loops, avoiding call stack buildup.

fields.question_text: 5. What is the time complexity of naive recursive Fibonacci calc(N) = calc(N-1) + calc(N-2)?
fields.explanation: Naive Fibonacci generates a binary call tree of height N, resulting in exponential O(2^N) calls due to redundant calculations.

fields.question_text: 6. What technique caches the results of expensive recursive calls to reduce time complexity from exponential to linear?
fields.explanation: Memoization stores subproblem solutions in a hash map/array, reusing cached answers in O(1) time.

fields.question_text: 7. What recurrence relation T(N) = 2 T(N/2) + O(N) represents Merge Sort?
fields.explanation: By Master Theorem case 2, dividing into 2 halves with linear merge cost yields O(N log N) time.

fields.question_text: 8. In Master Theorem formula T(N) = a T(N/b) + f(N), what does 'a' represent?
fields.option_b: Number of recursive subproblems generated at each step
fields.explanation: 'a' is the number of subproblems spawned in each recursive step (a >= 1).

fields.question_text: 9. What is the space complexity due to call stack for depth-first recursion of max tree height H?
fields.explanation: The call stack holds at most H stack frames simultaneously at any point along a branch path.

fields.question_text: 10. What is the general 3-step paradigm of Backtracking algorithms?
fields.explanation: Backtracking explores state space trees by choosing a path, recursing, and reverting state upon reaching dead ends.

fields.question_text: 11. How many total permutations are explored in brute force recursion for an array of size N?
fields.explanation: Placing N distinct elements in N slots generates N * (N-1) * ... * 1 = N! total permutations.

fields.question_text: 12. How many subsets (power set) exist for a set of size N?
fields.explanation: Each element has 2 options (include or exclude), yielding 2^N total subsets.

fields.question_text: 13. In N-Queens problem on N x N board, what technique prunes invalid search branches early?
fields.explanation: Tracking occupied columns and diagonals in O(1) lookup sets prunes illegal queen placements immediately.

fields.question_text: 14. In Sudoku Solver algorithm, what type of search strategy is utilized?
fields.explanation: DFS with Backtracking fills empty cells recursively, backspacing when digit conflicts occur.

fields.question_text: 15. What is the difference between Direct and Indirect Recursion?
fields.option_a: Direct calls itself; Indirect function A calls function B which calls A
fields.option_b: Direct uses stack; Indirect uses heap
fields.explanation: Direct recursion invokes the same function; Indirect recursion forms a cycle of function calls (A -> B -> A).

fields.question_text: 16. In Tower of Hanoi problem with N disks, what is the minimum number of moves required?
fields.explanation: The recurrence T(N) = 2 T(N-1) + 1 resolves to T(N) = 2^N - 1 total moves.

fields.question_text: 17. What is the time complexity of Quick Select algorithm (find Kth smallest element) on average?
fields.explanation: Recurrence T(N) = T(N/2) + O(N) sums N + N/2 + N/4 + ... = O(N) average time complexity.

fields.question_text: 18. How can any recursive algorithm be converted into an non-recursive iterative algorithm?
fields.option_a: Using an explicit Stack data structure to simulate function call frames
fields.explanation: Simulating the call stack using a custom Stack data structure converts any recursion to an iterative loop.

fields.question_text: 19. In Subset Sum problem (find subset summing to K), what is the time complexity of naive recursive backtracking?
fields.explanation: Exploring include/exclude decisions for N elements forms a binary recursion tree of size 2^N.

fields.question_text: 20. What is 'Branch and Bound' in optimization problems?
fields.option_b: Backtracking enhanced with upper/lower heuristic bounds to prune non-optimal subtrees
fields.explanation: Branch & Bound calculates cost bounds for state nodes, abandoning branches that cannot beat current best solution.

fields.question_text: 21. What happens to local variables of a function when a recursive call is invoked?
fields.option_b: Pushed onto stack in new stack frame, preserving caller variables independently
fields.explanation: Every invocation receives a distinct stack frame storing its own independent copy of local variables.

fields.question_text: 22. In Combination Sum problem (reuse numbers allowed), how do you prevent duplicate combinations in output?
fields.option_a: Sort array and start inner recursive loop from current index i instead of 0
fields.explanation: Passing start index i prevents choosing previously considered elements, avoiding duplicate combinations.

fields.question_text: 23. What is the time complexity of Word Search grid puzzle (word len L on M x N grid)?
fields.explanation: For each of M*N cells, exploring 3 direction branches up to depth L takes O(M * N * 3^L) worst case.

fields.question_text: 24. In recursive binary search T(N) = T(N/2) + O(1), what is the maximum call stack depth for N elements?
fields.explanation: Halving search space at each call limits stack depth to floor(log2 N) + 1 frames.

fields.question_text: 25. Which problem cannot be solved using simple divide-and-conquer without memoization/tabulation due to overlapping subproblems?
fields.explanation: LCS contains overlapping subproblems; pure divide-and-conquer leads to exponential re-computation without caching.

fields.question_text: 1. What is the primary advantage of a Linked List over a static Array?
fields.option_b: Dynamic size allocation without contiguous memory requirements
fields.explanation: Linked list nodes are allocated dynamically on heap; elements do not require contiguous memory blocks.

fields.question_text: 2. What is the time complexity to insert a new node at the HEAD of a Singly Linked List?
fields.explanation: Updating new_node->next = head and head = new_node requires constant O(1) pointer updates.

fields.question_text: 3. What is the time complexity to access the K-th element in a Singly Linked List of N nodes?
fields.explanation: Linked lists lack index memory formulas; accessing index K requires traversing K pointers sequentially.

fields.question_text: 4. What pointers are stored in each node of a Doubly Linked List?
fields.explanation: Doubly linked list nodes contain 'data', 'next' pointer (forward), and 'prev' pointer (backward).

fields.question_text: 5. What algorithm reverses a Singly Linked List in-place in O(N) time and O(1) space?
fields.explanation: Maintaining prev, curr, and next pointers redirects curr->next = prev in a single O(N) linear pass.

fields.question_text: 6. What is Floyd's Cycle Detection Algorithm (Tortoise & Hare)?
fields.option_a: Two pointers moving at same speed
fields.option_b: Slow pointer (1 step) and Fast pointer (2 steps) detect loops if they meet
fields.explanation: If a cycle exists, fast pointer catches slow pointer inside the loop in O(N) time and O(1) space.

fields.question_text: 7. After Floyd's algorithm detects a cycle, how do you locate the EXACT START NODE of the cycle?
fields.option_a: Reset fast to Head, keep slow at meeting point, move both 1 step at a time until they collide
fields.explanation: Distance from head to cycle start equals distance from meeting point to cycle start along loop path.

fields.question_text: 8. What is the purpose of a 'Dummy Head Node' in linked list operations?
fields.option_b: Simplifies boundary conditions when inserting/deleting list head
fields.explanation: Dummy node eliminates special edge-case checks when head node is modified or deleted.

fields.question_text: 9. How do fast and slow pointers find the MIDDLE node of a linked list in one pass?
fields.option_a: Fast moves 1 step, slow moves 2 steps
fields.option_b: Fast moves 2 steps, slow moves 1 step; when fast reaches end, slow is at middle
fields.explanation: Because fast travels twice as fast, slow arrives at middle node when fast reaches the end.

fields.question_text: 10. What is the time and space complexity to find the K-th node from the END of a linked list using two pointers?
fields.option_c: O(N log N) time, O(1) space
fields.explanation: Advance pointer1 by K steps first, then advance pointer1 and pointer2 together until pointer1 reaches NULL.

fields.question_text: 11. How does a Circular Linked List differ from a standard Singly Linked List?
fields.option_a: Last node's next pointer points back to Head instead of NULL
fields.explanation: In circular linked lists, tail->next points to head node, forming a continuous circular chain.

fields.question_text: 12. What is the time complexity to delete a node given ONLY a direct pointer 'node' to it in a Singly Linked List (not tail)?
fields.option_b: O(1) by copying node->next data into node and deleting node->next
fields.explanation: Copy next node's val into current node, then point node->next = node->next->next and delete node->next in O(1).

fields.question_text: 13. What is the time complexity of Merge Sort on a Linked List of size N?
fields.explanation: Merge Sort splits list using middle pointer O(N) and merges sorted sublists in O(N log N) time & O(1) aux space.

fields.question_text: 14. Why is Quick Sort less preferred than Merge Sort for Singly Linked Lists?
fields.option_a: Quick sort requires random access indexing arr[i]
fields.option_c: Merge sort requires O(N) extra array space
fields.explanation: Quick Sort relies on efficient random access pointer jumps; Merge Sort only requires sequential pointer relinking.

fields.question_text: 15. In LRU Cache implementation, why is a Doubly Linked List used alongside a Hash Map?
fields.option_a: Allows O(1) removal and node relocation to head upon access
fields.explanation: Doubly linked list allows removing any node in O(1) given its pointer, enabling O(1) LRU updates.

fields.question_text: 16. What is a 'Skip List'?
fields.option_a: A linked list with missing nodes
fields.option_b: Probabilistic data structure using multi-level pointer forward tracks to achieve O(log N) search/insert
fields.explanation: Skip List builds hierarchy of express lane linked lists, achieving O(log N) search, insert, and delete.

fields.question_text: 17. What is an 'XOR Doubly Linked List'?
fields.option_a: Memory-optimized doubly linked list storing XOR address (prev ^ next) in a single pointer field
fields.explanation: Node stores pointer_diff = prev ^ next, saving half the pointer memory overhead per node.

fields.question_text: 18. What is the time complexity to check if a Singly Linked List is a Palindrome using fast/slow pointers and reversing second half?
fields.option_c: O(N log N) time, O(1) space
fields.explanation: Find middle (fast/slow), reverse second half, compare halves, and restore list in linear O(N) time & O(1) space.

fields.question_text: 19. How do you find the Intersection Node of two linked lists of lengths M and N in O(M+N) time and O(1) space?
fields.option_b: Two pointers pA and pB; when pA hits end jump to headB, when pB hits end jump to headA
fields.explanation: Traversing lenA + lenB equalizes path lengths, causing pointers to meet at intersection node in O(M+N).

fields.question_text: 20. What is the time complexity of merging K sorted linked lists of total N nodes using Min-Heap?
fields.explanation: Min-heap of size K extracts minimum node and inserts next node in O(log K) time per node across N nodes.

fields.question_text: 21. What happens if you fail to update tail->next = NULL when splitting a linked list into two sublists?
fields.explanation: Failing to terminate sublist tail pointer with NULL leaves sublist linked to original list tail.

fields.question_text: 22. In Copy List with Random Pointer problem, how can you clone the list in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space?
fields.option_a: Interleave cloned nodes next to original nodes (A -> A' -> B -> B')
fields.explanation: Interleaving cloned nodes allows setting clone->random = original->random->next without extra hash map.

fields.question_text: 23. Why do Linked Lists experience worse hardware performance than Arrays during sequential traversal?
fields.option_b: Heap memory fragmentation causes high CPU Cache Misses
fields.explanation: Scattered node pointers break spatial cache locality, requiring individual memory fetches on cache misses.

fields.question_text: 24. What is the time complexity of Flattening a Multi-Level Doubly Linked List containing child pointers?
fields.option_a: O(N) where N is total nodes
fields.explanation: Using stack or tail pointer relinking, each node and child pointer is processed once in linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 25. How do Lock-Free Concurrent Linked Lists perform thread-safe insertions without global mutexes?
fields.explanation: Atomic CAS operations update node pointers atomically, retrying if concurrent threads modify target pointer.

fields.question_text: 1. What operational principle governs a Stack data structure?
fields.explanation: Stack enforces Last-In, First-Out: the most recently pushed element is the first element popped.

fields.question_text: 2. What is the time complexity of Push, Pop, and Top operations in a standard Stack?
fields.explanation: All basic stack operations target the top element index/pointer, executing in constant O(1) time.

fields.question_text: 3. What condition occurs when attempting to POP an element from an EMPTY stack?
fields.explanation: Popping or peeking from an empty stack triggers a Stack Underflow error.

fields.question_text: 4. What runtime environment structure tracks function calls, local variables, and return addresses?
fields.explanation: The system call stack pushes frame on function invocation and pops frame upon return.

fields.question_text: 5. What algorithm converts Infix mathematical expressions (A + B) to Postfix (A B +)?
fields.explanation: Dijkstra's Shunting-Yard algorithm uses an operator stack to parse infix expressions into postfix notation.

fields.question_text: 6. How is postfix expression '3 4 + 2 *' evaluated using a stack?
fields.option_a: Result = 14: push 3, 4; '+' pops 3+4=7, push 7; push 2; '*' pops 7*2=14
fields.explanation: Operands are pushed; operators pop 2 operands, calculate result, and push back. (3+4)*2 = 14.

fields.question_text: 7. How can you design a Min-Stack where getMin() runs in O(1) time?
fields.option_b: Maintain auxiliary stack storing current minimum value at each depth
fields.explanation: Auxiliary stack tracks min(val, auxStack.top()), enabling O(1) getMin() alongside standard stack operations.

fields.question_text: 8. What pattern uses a stack maintaining elements in strictly increasing/decreasing order to find Next Greater Element?
fields.explanation: Monotonic stack pops smaller elements when encountering larger incoming element, solving Next Greater in O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 9. What is the time complexity to solve 'Next Greater Element' for all N array elements using a Monotonic Stack?
fields.explanation: Each element is pushed once and popped at most once, taking amortized linear O(N) total time.

fields.question_text: 10. In 'Valid Parentheses' problem, what action is taken when encountering a closing bracket ')'?
fields.option_b: Pop top element and check if it matches corresponding opening bracket '('
fields.explanation: Closing brackets must match the most recently pushed opening bracket at stack top.

fields.question_text: 11. What is the time complexity to calculate Largest Rectangle in Histogram using a Monotonic Stack?
fields.explanation: Monotonic increasing stack determines left and right smaller boundary spans in linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 12. In Daily Temperatures problem (days until warmer temperature), what does the stack store?
fields.option_b: Indices of array elements in monotonic decreasing temperature order
fields.explanation: Storing indices allows computing day distance i - stack.pop() when warmer temperature arrives.

fields.question_text: 13. How can a Queue be implemented using TWO Stacks (inStack & outStack)?
fields.option_a: Enqueue pushes to inStack; Dequeue pops outStack (transferring inStack to outStack if empty)
fields.explanation: Transferring elements reverses stack order into FIFO order. Dequeue runs in amortized O(1) time.

fields.question_text: 14. What is the space complexity of an Array-based Stack of capacity C?
fields.explanation: Allocating contiguous array buffer of fixed size C consumes O(C) memory space.

fields.question_text: 15. What is the time complexity of reversing a string using a Stack?
fields.explanation: Pushing all N characters then popping them back reverses string in linear O(N) time & space.

fields.question_text: 16. In expression parsing, prefix notation '+ A B' is also known as:
fields.explanation: Prefix notation is called Polish Notation; Postfix notation is called Reverse Polish Notation (RPN).

fields.question_text: 17. In Maximal Rectangle in 2D Binary Matrix problem, how is the problem transformed to use Histogram Stack algorithm?
fields.option_a: Treat each row as histogram base by accumulating consecutive 1s vertically
fields.explanation: Updating running height array per row converts 2D matrix max rectangle into N subproblems of Histogram O(R * C).

fields.question_text: 18. What stack state indicates that a string of brackets is valid after processing all characters?
fields.explanation: An empty stack confirms all opened brackets were successfully matched and closed in proper order.

fields.question_text: 19. In Asteroid Collision problem, when two asteroids meet (positive moving right, negative moving left), what determines which survives?
fields.option_a: Asteroid with larger absolute size survives; equal sizes explode both
fields.explanation: Top asteroid on stack collides with incoming asteroid until size comparison resolves or direction changes.

fields.question_text: 20. How do you implement stack using a SINGLE Queue recursively?
fields.option_a: On push(x), enqueue x, then dequeue and re-enqueue previous N-1 elements
fields.explanation: Rotating previous N-1 elements behind incoming element x moves x to queue front (LIFO ordering).

fields.question_text: 21. What is the auxiliary space complexity of removing adjacent duplicates in a string using stack?
fields.explanation: Stack maintains non-duplicate character sequence of length up to N, consuming O(N) space.

fields.question_text: 22. In Decode String ('3[a2[c]]' -> 'accaccacc'), what data structure handles nested bracket expansion?
fields.explanation: Stacks save multiplier counts and current string prefixes when entering nested brackets '['.

fields.question_text: 23. In Simplify Path problem ('/a/./b/../../c/'), what does '..' command perform on path stack?
fields.option_b: Pop top directory from stack if stack non-empty
fields.explanation: '..' represents parent directory, popping most recent directory from path stack.

fields.question_text: 24. What is the time complexity of evaluating an RPN (Reverse Polish Notation) expression array of length N?
fields.explanation: Scanning array once while pushing operands and popping for operators executes in linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 25. Which OS memory segment grows downward towards lower memory addresses on x86 architectures?
fields.explanation: The call stack segment conventionally grows downward from high memory addresses toward lower addresses.

fields.question_text: 1. What ordering invariant defines a Queue data structure?
fields.explanation: Queue operates under First-In, First-Out: elements are inserted at rear and removed from front.

fields.question_text: 2. What are the core operations of a Queue called?
fields.explanation: Enqueue adds elements to queue rear; Dequeue removes elements from queue front in O(1) time.

fields.question_text: 3. In a simple array-based queue without circular indexing, what is the drawback of Dequeue?
fields.option_b: Unused empty slots at front remain wasted unless elements shift in O(N) time
fields.explanation: Incrementing front pointer leaves front array slots empty and inaccessible unless elements shift (O(N)).

fields.question_text: 4. What formula updates the rear pointer in a Circular Queue of size N?
fields.explanation: Modulo arithmetic wraps rear pointer back to index 0 when reaching array end.

fields.question_text: 5. How do you distinguish between EMPTY and FULL states in a Circular Queue of size N using front and rear?
fields.option_a: Empty: count == 0; Full: count == N (or maintain size counter)
fields.explanation: Tracking current element count variable distinguishes empty (count=0) from full (count=N) unequivocally.

fields.question_text: 6. What is a Deque (Double-Ended Queue)?
fields.option_a: Queue allowing insertion and deletion at BOTH front and rear ends in O(1)
fields.explanation: Deque supports push_front, push_back, pop_front, and pop_back all in constant O(1) time.

fields.question_text: 7. What graph traversal algorithm relies fundamentally on a Queue data structure?
fields.explanation: BFS uses FIFO queue to explore graph vertices level-by-level in order of distance from source.

fields.question_text: 8. What data structure underpins a Priority Queue to achieve O(log N) insertion and extraction of min/max element?
fields.explanation: Binary Heap maintains heap-order property in tree structure, enabling O(log N) push and pop.

fields.question_text: 9. In Sliding Window Maximum problem (array size N, window K), what data structure achieves linear O(N) overall time?
fields.option_b: Monotonic Decreasing Deque storing element indices
fields.explanation: Monotonic Deque removes smaller elements from rear and outdated indices from front in O(N) total time.

fields.question_text: 10. How can a Stack be implemented using TWO Queues (q1 & q2)?
fields.option_a: Push to q2, transfer all elements from q1 to q2, swap q1 and q2 names
fields.explanation: Re-queueing existing elements behind incoming element reverses FIFO order into LIFO order.

fields.question_text: 11. In Multi-Source BFS (e.g. Rotting Oranges), how is the Queue initialized before loop execution?
fields.option_b: Push ALL initial rotten orange coordinates into queue simultaneously at t=0
fields.explanation: Enqueuing all starting points at level 0 expands distance frontiers simultaneously in parallel.

fields.question_text: 12. In OS CPU process scheduling, what queue mechanism prevents low-priority processes from starving?
fields.option_b: Multilevel Feedback Queue with Aging (boosting priority over time)
fields.explanation: Multilevel feedback queues adjust priorities dynamically, aging waiting tasks to guarantee execution.

fields.question_text: 13. What is the time complexity to find Kth largest element in array using Min-Heap of size K?
fields.explanation: Maintaining size-K min-heap takes O(log K) for each of N array insertions, yielding O(N log K).

fields.question_text: 14. What is a 'Lock-Free SPSC Ring Buffer'?
fields.option_a: Single Producer Single Consumer circular queue using atomic atomic head/tail pointers without mutex locks
fields.explanation: SPSC ring buffer allows 1 thread writing and 1 thread reading without lock contention.

fields.question_text: 15. In Circular Tour / Gas Station problem, what is the time complexity to find starting station completing circuit?
fields.option_b: O(N) time and O(1) space using running tank balance queue logic
fields.explanation: Single pass accumulating total gas vs cost finds starting gas station in linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 16. What is the time complexity of popping the highest priority element from an UNORDERED Array implementation of Priority Queue?
fields.explanation: Inserting takes O(1), but finding and removing maximum element from unsorted array requires scanning all N elements O(N).

fields.question_text: 17. In standard C++ STL, what data structure underlies std::queue by default?
fields.explanation: std::deque provides contiguous chunk memory with O(1) push/pop at both front and back.

fields.question_text: 18. What is the time complexity of building a Binary Heap from an array of N elements (Heapify)?
fields.explanation: Bottom-up heapify sums node heights sum(N / 2^(h+1) * h) = linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 19. In Task Scheduler problem (with cooling period CPU tasks), what data structures are optimal?
fields.option_a: Max-Heap for frequencies and Queue for cooling timer
fields.explanation: Max-heap picks highest frequency task; queue holds cooling tasks until ready time arrives.

fields.question_text: 20. What is the time complexity to peek front element in a Queue?
fields.explanation: Peeking returns element at front pointer/index in constant O(1) time without modifying queue.

fields.question_text: 21. How do you implement a Stream Moving Average of last K integers?
fields.option_a: Queue of size K tracking running sum; subtract popped element when size exceeds K
fields.explanation: Queue maintains latest K elements; running_sum += val - queue.dequeue() calculates average in O(1).

fields.question_text: 22. In 0-1 BFS (graph edge weights 0 or 1), what data structure replaces Priority Queue to achieve O(V + E) time?
fields.option_a: Deque (push front weight 0, push back weight 1)
fields.explanation: Deque maintains sorted distance order by adding 0-weight edges at front and 1-weight edges at back in O(1).

fields.question_text: 23. In Priority Queue, what operation decreases the key value of an existing node in Fibonacci Heap in amortized O(1) time?
fields.explanation: Fibonacci Heaps support amortized O(1) Decrease-Key, improving Dijkstra's algorithm to O(E + V log V).

fields.question_text: 24. What happens when enqueueing to a Queue that has reached max capacity?
fields.explanation: Attempting to push element into full queue triggers Queue Overflow error.

fields.question_text: 25. Which problem is solved in O(N) using Monotonic Queue of sliding window?
fields.explanation: Monotonic Queue maintains window extremes in O(1) amortized time per element slide across array.

fields.question_text: 1. What is the main advantage of Sliding Window technique over brute force nested loops?
fields.option_a: Reduces time complexity from O(N^2) or O(N^3) to linear O(N)
fields.explanation: Sliding window updates sub-segment state incrementally in O(1) instead of re-scanning window contents.

fields.question_text: 2. In Fixed-Size Sliding Window of length K, how is running window sum updated when moving window right by 1 step?
fields.explanation: Add entering right element and subtract leaving left element in constant O(1) time.

fields.question_text: 3. In Dynamic-Size Sliding Window (e.g. Max Subarray Sum <= Target with positive numbers), when do you expand right pointer R?
fields.option_a: When window condition is valid, expand R to find larger window
fields.explanation: Expand R to test larger valid window bounds; shrink L when window constraint is violated.

fields.question_text: 4. What is the time complexity of processing an array of size N using Dynamic Sliding Window where left L and right R pointers move forward?
fields.option_b: O(N) because L and R each advance at most N steps
fields.explanation: L and R pointers move monotonically forward from 0 to N; total operations bounded by 2N = O(N).

fields.question_text: 5. In sorted array Two Pointer inward convergence (e.g. 2Sum), if arr[L] + arr[R] > Target, what action is taken?
fields.explanation: Because array is sorted, decrementing R reduces total sum closer to target value.

fields.question_text: 6. Why can standard Sliding Window NOT be applied directly to solve Subarray Sum Equals K when array contains NEGATIVE numbers?
fields.option_a: Window sum is non-monotonic (expanding R may decrease sum, shrinking L may increase sum)
fields.explanation: Sliding window requires monotonicity (expanding increases sum). For negative numbers, Prefix Sum + Hash Map solves problem in O(N).

fields.question_text: 7. What formula calculates exact count of subarrays with EXACTLY K distinct elements using At-Most helper function?
fields.explanation: Subarrays with at most K distinct minus subarrays with at most K-1 distinct leaves subarrays with exactly K distinct.

fields.question_text: 8. What is the time complexity of finding Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters using sliding window & hash map?
fields.explanation: Updating character last-seen index map allows shrinking left boundary L in single pass linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 9. In Minimum Window Substring (string S len N, target T len M), what is the optimal overall time complexity?
fields.explanation: Sliding window on S maintaining frequency count match of T processes each string character in O(N + M) time.

fields.question_text: 10. In Fruit Into Baskets problem (at most 2 distinct fruit types in window), what determines window shrinking trigger?
fields.explanation: Shrink left pointer L until distinct count in frequency map drops back to 2.

fields.question_text: 11. In Fast and Slow Pointers (Floyd's Tortoise & Hare) for array duplicate detection (Find Duplicate Number), why does it run in O(1) space?
fields.option_a: Array values act as next pointers arr[i]
fields.explanation: Treating index i -> arr[i] as linked list node links forms a cycle containing the duplicate number.

fields.question_text: 12. In Container With Most Water problem (height array), how do you decide which pointer L or R to move inward?
fields.option_a: Move pointer with SMALLER height (height[L] < height[R] ? L++ : R--)
fields.explanation: Area is constrained by shorter line. Moving shorter line offers only opportunity to discover taller boundary.

fields.question_text: 13. In Max Consecutive Ones III (flip at most K zeros), what does window store?
fields.option_a: Running count of zeros inside window [L, R] <= K
fields.explanation: Window expands R; when zero_count > K, advance L until zero_count <= K.

fields.question_text: 14. In 3Sum problem (find triplets sum to 0), why is array sorted first?
fields.option_a: Enables Two Pointer inward convergence and easy skip of duplicate elements
fields.explanation: Sorting array in O(N log N) allows 2 pointers per outer element and skipping duplicate values seamlessly.

fields.question_text: 15. What is the time complexity of 4Sum problem optimized with 2 outer loops and inner 2-pointer convergence?
fields.explanation: Two nested loops take O(N^2); inner 2 pointers scan remaining range in O(N), yielding total O(N^3).

fields.question_text: 16. In Subarrays with Bounded Maximum (max element between L and R), how is count accumulated?
fields.option_a: Track last valid element index within range [L, R]
fields.explanation: Updating position indices of elements in range accumulated count in linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 17. In Minimum Size Subarray Sum (sum >= Target with positive numbers), what is updated upon finding a valid window sum?
fields.option_a: min_len = min(min_len, R - L + 1), then shrink L to test smaller window
fields.explanation: Record minimum window length, then subtract arr[L] and increment L to seek shorter valid subarray.

fields.question_text: 18. How many total subarrays of window size K exist in array of size N?
fields.explanation: Window slides from starting index 0 up to index N - K, producing exactly N - K + 1 windows.

fields.question_text: 19. In Permutation in String problem (check if S1 permutation is substring of S2), what window size is maintained on S2?
fields.option_a: Fixed window of size equal to length of S1
fields.explanation: Permutations have identical length; slide fixed window of size len(S1) across S2 comparing char frequencies.

fields.question_text: 20. In Trapping Rain Water problem using Two Pointers (left & right), what metric determines water trapped at index?
fields.explanation: Water level at index i is bounded by minimum of tallest left and right walls minus current bar height.

fields.question_text: 21. In Move Zeroes to end in-place, how do slow and fast pointers operate?
fields.option_a: Fast scans array; when arr[fast] != 0, swap arr[slow] and arr[fast], increment slow
fields.explanation: Slow pointer tracks target write position for non-zero numbers in single linear O(N) pass.

fields.question_text: 22. What is the space complexity of Two Pointer inward algorithm on sorted array?
fields.explanation: Two pointer convergence uses only two integer index variables, requiring O(1) auxiliary space.

fields.question_text: 23. In Longest Repeating Character Replacement (replace at most K chars), window is valid if:
fields.explanation: Remaining characters to flip (window length minus most frequent character count) must not exceed K.

fields.question_text: 24. In Subarray Product Less Than K (positive integers), how many valid subarrays end at index R?
fields.explanation: For valid window [L, R], all contiguous subarrays ending at R (lengths 1 to R-L+1) are valid, adding R-L+1.

fields.question_text: 25. What is the optimal time complexity to find Partition Labels (partition string into max parts where char appears in 1 part)?
fields.explanation: Record last occurrence index of each character, then expand window boundary max_last in single O(N) pass.

fields.question_text: 1. What is the defining topological property of a Tree with N vertices?
fields.option_a: Connected acyclic graph with exactly N - 1 edges
fields.explanation: A tree is a connected acyclic graph containing exactly N vertices and N-1 edges.

fields.question_text: 2. What is the Depth of a node in a tree?
fields.option_a: Number of edges on the path from Root to that node
fields.option_b: Number of edges on longest path from node to a leaf
fields.explanation: Depth measure distance from Root (depth 0) down to target node.

fields.question_text: 3. What is the Height of a tree?
fields.option_a: Number of edges on the longest path from Root to any Leaf node
fields.explanation: Height is maximum depth among all leaf nodes in the tree.

fields.question_text: 4. In binary tree Depth-First Search, what is the order of nodes visited in INORDER Traversal?
fields.explanation: Inorder recursively visits Left Subtree, Root node, then Right Subtree.

fields.question_text: 5. In binary tree Depth-First Search, what is the order of nodes visited in PREORDER Traversal?
fields.explanation: Preorder visits Root node first, then recursively Left Subtree, then Right Subtree.

fields.question_text: 6. In binary tree Depth-First Search, what is the order of nodes visited in POSTORDER Traversal?
fields.explanation: Postorder recursively visits Left Subtree, Right Subtree, and finally Root node.

fields.question_text: 7. What data structure is used to perform Level-Order Traversal (BFS) of a tree?
fields.explanation: Level-order traversal uses a FIFO queue to visit nodes level-by-level top-to-bottom.

fields.question_text: 8. What is the maximum number of nodes in a Binary Tree of height H (where root height = 0)?
fields.explanation: Summing 1 + 2 + 4 + ... + 2^H geometric series yields 2^(H+1) - 1 maximum nodes.

fields.question_text: 9. What is a 'Full Binary Tree'?
fields.option_a: Tree where every node has either 0 or 2 children
fields.option_b: Tree where all leaves are at same depth
fields.explanation: In a Full Binary Tree, no node has exactly 1 child (nodes have either 0 or 2 children).

fields.question_text: 10. What is a 'Complete Binary Tree'?
fields.option_a: Binary tree where every level is completely filled except possibly last level, which is filled from left to right
fields.explanation: Complete binary trees fill levels left-to-right, making them ideal for array representation in heaps.

fields.question_text: 11. What is the Diameter of a Binary Tree?
fields.option_a: Length of longest path between ANY two nodes in the tree (may or may not pass through root)
fields.explanation: Diameter is max(left_height + right_height) evaluated at every node in postorder traversal.

fields.question_text: 12. What pair of tree traversals is required to UNLEASH unique reconstruction of a general Binary Tree?
fields.explanation: Inorder traversal is essential because it splits nodes into left and right subtrees around root node identified by Preorder/Postorder.

fields.question_text: 13. What is the time complexity to check if a binary tree is Symmetric (mirror image of itself)?
fields.explanation: Recursive DFS comparing left.left vs right.right and left.right vs right.left visits each node once in O(N).

fields.question_text: 14. In Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum problem, what does a node return to its parent during postorder recursion?
fields.explanation: Parent can choose at most ONE child branch path to extend; returning max non-negative branch path allows parent path continuation.

fields.question_text: 15. What is Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) of two nodes P and Q in a general binary tree?
fields.option_a: Deepest node that has both P and Q as descendants
fields.explanation: LCA is the deepest shared ancestor node along paths from root to P and root to Q.

fields.question_text: 16. What is the time complexity of finding LCA in a balanced Binary Tree of N nodes?
fields.explanation: Recursive DFS visiting nodes to locate P and Q scans up to N nodes in O(N) worst case.

fields.question_text: 17. What is Morris Inorder Traversal?
fields.option_a: Inorder traversal achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space using threaded temporary links to predecessor
fields.explanation: Morris traversal creates temporary threads from rightmost child of left subtree back to current root node, avoiding call stack.

fields.question_text: 18. What is the space complexity of recursive DFS traversal on a SKEWED tree of N nodes?
fields.explanation: A degenerate line tree of height N creates N recursive call stack frames.

fields.question_text: 19. In Zigzag Level-Order Traversal (Spiral Order), how are level node values accumulated?
fields.option_a: Alternate left-to-right and right-to-left insertion direction per level
fields.explanation: Flips insertion order (normal vs reversed) on alternating level indices.

fields.question_text: 20. How do you serialize a binary tree into a string for storage?
fields.option_a: Preorder traversal inserting null markers '#' for missing child pointers
fields.explanation: Preorder with null markers unambiguously encodes tree structure for exact deserialization.

fields.question_text: 21. What is the maximum number of leaf nodes in a Full Binary Tree with L leaves?
fields.explanation: In full binary trees, internal nodes I = L - 1, so total nodes N = I + L = 2L - 1.

fields.question_text: 22. In Path Sum III (count paths summing to Target, path does not need to start at root), what optimal data structure is used during DFS?
fields.explanation: Tracking running root-to-node prefix sum counts in hash map finds valid sub-paths in O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 23. In Subtree of Another Tree problem, what is the worst-case time complexity comparing tree S (N nodes) and T (M nodes)?
fields.explanation: Comparing subtree structure at each of N nodes takes O(M), giving O(N * M) worst case.

fields.question_text: 24. What is the time complexity to flatten a binary tree into a linked list in-place using right pointer chaining?
fields.explanation: Re-linking left subtree between root and right subtree processes each node in linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 25. Which traversal visits all leaf nodes from left to right in a standard binary tree?
fields.option_a: Inorder, Preorder, and Postorder all visit leaves in left-to-right relative order
fields.explanation: DFS traversals preserve left-to-right child exploration priority, visiting leaf nodes in left-to-right order.

fields.question_text: 1. What is the defining constraint of a Binary Tree?
fields.option_a: Every node has at most 2 children (left child and right child)
fields.option_c: Tree height must be log N
fields.explanation: Binary tree degree is bounded by 2: each node has 0, 1, or 2 children.

fields.question_text: 2. What is a 'Perfect Binary Tree'?
fields.option_a: Binary tree where all internal nodes have 2 children AND all leaf nodes are at identical depth
fields.explanation: Perfect binary trees are completely filled across all levels with total nodes = 2^(H+1) - 1.

fields.question_text: 3. In an array representation of a Complete Binary Tree (1-based indexing), what is the index of the LEFT child of node at index i?
fields.explanation: 1-based array heap indexing maps left child to 2*i, right child to 2*i + 1, parent to i // 2.

fields.question_text: 4. In 0-based array indexing of a Complete Binary Tree, what is the index of the RIGHT child of node at index i?
fields.explanation: 0-based indexing maps left child = 2*i + 1, right child = 2*i + 2, parent = (i - 1) // 2.

fields.question_text: 5. What algorithm calculates Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree?
fields.option_a: BFS Level-Order maintaining horizontal distance HD (left HD-1, right HD+1) in Map
fields.explanation: Assigning HD column coordinates and grouping node values by HD column via BFS computes vertical view.

fields.question_text: 6. In Top View of a Binary Tree, which node is visible for each vertical column HD?
fields.option_a: The FIRST node encountered at column HD during BFS level-order traversal
fields.explanation: Top view retains the highest level (first seen) node for each horizontal distance coordinate HD.

fields.question_text: 7. In Bottom View of a Binary Tree, which node is visible for each vertical column HD?
fields.option_a: The LAST node encountered at column HD during BFS level-order traversal
fields.explanation: Bottom view overwrites map entry so the lowest level (last seen) node per column HD remains.

fields.question_text: 8. In Left View of a Binary Tree, which nodes are visible?
fields.option_a: The first node encountered at each level depth during BFS level-order
fields.explanation: Left view captures the leftmost node (first node processed per level during BFS).

fields.question_text: 9. In Right View of a Binary Tree, which nodes are visible?
fields.option_a: The last node encountered at each level depth during BFS level-order
fields.explanation: Right view captures the rightmost node (last node processed per level depth during BFS).

fields.question_text: 10. What is the time complexity to check if a binary tree is Height-Balanced (AVL balanced property |left_h - right_h| <= 1)?
fields.option_a: O(N) using bottom-up postorder returning height or -1 if unbalanced
fields.explanation: Bottom-up postorder computes height and short-circuits with -1 if balance factor fails, taking O(N).

fields.question_text: 11. What is the Maximum Width of a Binary Tree?
fields.option_a: Maximum width among all levels, measured as positional distance between leftmost and rightmost non-null nodes in level
fields.explanation: Width uses positional heap indexing per level: (rightmost_index - leftmost_index + 1).

fields.question_text: 12. In Invert/Flip Binary Tree (mirror image), what operation is performed at each node?
fields.option_a: Swap node.left and node.right pointers recursively
fields.explanation: Swapping left and right child pointers at every node mirrors the tree structure in O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 13. What is the total number of structurally unique Binary Trees that can be formed with N unlabeled nodes?
fields.explanation: The N-th Catalan number C_n counts structurally unique unlabeled binary tree topologies.

fields.question_text: 14. How many structurally unique Binary Search Trees can be formed with N distinct key values?
fields.explanation: With keys sorted, choosing root i leaves C_(i-1) left subtrees and C_(n-i) right subtrees, producing C_n total BSTs.

fields.question_text: 15. In Boundary Traversal of a Binary Tree, in what order are boundary nodes collected?
fields.option_a: Root -> Left Boundary (excluding leaves) -> All Leaf Nodes -> Right Boundary in Reverse (excluding leaves)
fields.explanation: Boundary traversal collects outer perimeter nodes counter-clockwise: Root, Left edge, Leaves, Right edge reverse.

fields.question_text: 16. What is the time complexity of Boundary Traversal on a tree of N nodes?
fields.explanation: Left boundary O(H), leaves DFS O(N), and right boundary O(H) combine to linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 17. What is an 'Expression Tree'?
fields.option_a: Binary tree where internal nodes are operators (+, -, *, /) and leaves are operands
fields.explanation: Inorder traversal of expression tree yields infix math statement; Postorder yields postfix RPN.

fields.question_text: 18. In Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Postorder Traversal, when is construction unique?
fields.option_a: Only if the binary tree is FULL (every node has 0 or 2 children)
fields.explanation: Single-child nodes create ambiguity between preorder/postorder; unique construction requires full binary trees.

fields.question_text: 19. What is the auxiliary space complexity of Level-Order Traversal on a Perfect Binary Tree of height H (N nodes)?
fields.option_a: O(N) queue memory (max level contains ~N/2 leaf nodes)
fields.explanation: The bottom leaf level holds N/2 nodes simultaneously in the BFS queue, requiring O(N) space.

fields.question_text: 20. How do you find the All Nodes Distance K from Target Node in Binary Tree?
fields.option_a: Build parent pointer graph links during DFS, then run BFS outwards from target node up to distance K
fields.explanation: Mapping parent links converts binary tree into undirected graph; BFS expands distance K layer by layer.

fields.question_text: 21. What is the Maximum Path Sum between any two leaves in a binary tree?
fields.option_a: Postorder tracking max(max_leaf_path, left_path + right_path + node.val)
fields.explanation: Postorder recursion evaluates sum of left and right leaf paths passing through current node.

fields.question_text: 22. In Cousin Nodes in Binary Tree (same depth, different parents), how is relationship validated?
fields.option_a: Nodes P and Q have identical depth level AND node1.parent != node2.parent
fields.explanation: Cousins share the same depth level in tree hierarchy but possess distinct parent nodes.

fields.question_text: 23. In Population of Next Right Pointers in Each Node (Perfect Binary Tree), what pointer link is added?
fields.explanation: Leveraging existing next pointers connects level sibling nodes in O(1) extra space.

fields.question_text: 24. What is the time complexity to Count Complete Tree Nodes in less than O(N) time?
fields.option_a: O((log N)^2) by comparing left and right subtree heights to binary search complete level
fields.explanation: If left_h == right_h, left subtree is perfect (2^h - 1 nodes); recurse right. Runs in O((log N)^2) time.

fields.question_text: 25. Which tree property guarantees that simple array 2*i and 2*i+1 indexing stores nodes compactly without empty slot gaps?
fields.explanation: Complete binary trees fill levels left-to-right, ensuring array indices 0..N-1 are densely packed.

fields.question_text: 1. What is the structural ordering invariant of a Binary Search Tree (BST)?
fields.option_a: Left Subtree values < Root value < Right Subtree values for EVERY node
fields.option_c: Left subtree height == Right subtree height
fields.explanation: Every node in a BST strictly satisfies: all left descendants < node.val < all right descendants.

fields.question_text: 2. What tree traversal on a BST produces node key values in STRICTLY SORTED ascending order?
fields.explanation: Inorder traversal (Left, Root, Right) processes BST keys in monotonically increasing sorted order.

fields.question_text: 3. What is the time complexity of Search, Insert, and Delete in a BALANCED BST of N nodes?
fields.explanation: When tree height H = O(log N), binary decisions eliminate half the remaining tree at each step.

fields.question_text: 4. What is the WORST-CASE time complexity of searching in a SKEWED (degenerate) BST of N nodes?
fields.explanation: Inserting sorted elements into un-balanced BST builds a linear chain of height N, degrading operations to O(N).

fields.question_text: 5. In BST node DELETION, what replaces a deleted node that has TWO children?
fields.option_a: Inorder Successor (smallest node in right subtree) OR Inorder Predecessor (largest in left subtree)
fields.explanation: Replacing with Inorder Successor preserves the BST ordering invariant without breaking subtrees.

fields.question_text: 6. How do you locate the MINIMUM key value in a BST?
fields.option_a: Traverse left pointers starting from Root until node.left is NULL
fields.explanation: The minimum value resides at the leftmost node of the BST.

fields.question_text: 7. How do you locate the MAXIMUM key value in a BST?
fields.option_a: Traverse right pointers starting from Root until node.right is NULL
fields.explanation: The maximum value resides at the rightmost node of the BST.

fields.question_text: 8. How can you validate if a Binary Tree is a VALID BST in linear O(N) time?
fields.option_a: DFS passing valid range bounds (min_val, max_val) down to children
fields.option_b: Check node.left < node < node.right locally only
fields.explanation: Local checks fail for deep illegal descendants. DFS must enforce global range (min_val < node.val < max_val).

fields.question_text: 9. What is the time complexity to find K-th Smallest Element in a BST using Inorder Traversal?
fields.option_a: O(H + K) time, O(H) stack space
fields.explanation: Iterative Inorder traversal stops as soon as K nodes are visited, taking O(H + K) time.

fields.question_text: 10. In BST, how is Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) of nodes P and Q located efficiently in O(H) time?
fields.option_a: Starting from Root: if P and Q < curr, move left; if P and Q > curr, move right; else curr is LCA
fields.explanation: The first node where P and Q split into left and right subtrees (or match curr) is the LCA in BST.

fields.question_text: 11. What is the FLOOR value of Key X in a BST?
fields.option_a: The largest key value in the BST that is <= X
fields.explanation: Floor is the maximum node key smaller than or equal to target X.

fields.question_text: 12. What is the CEIL value of Key X in a BST?
fields.option_a: The smallest key value in the BST that is >= X
fields.explanation: Ceil is the minimum node key greater than or equal to target X.

fields.question_text: 13. How do you convert a Sorted Array into a Height-Balanced BST in O(N) time?
fields.option_a: Pick middle element arr[mid] as Root, recursively build left subtree from left half, right subtree from right half
fields.explanation: Picking mid element divides array evenly, creating an optimal AVL-balanced BST of height O(log N).

fields.question_text: 14. How do you convert a Sorted Doubly Linked List into a Balanced BST in-place in O(N) time?
fields.option_a: Bottom-up Inorder simulation advancing list head pointer as nodes are built
fields.explanation: Bottom-up construction builds left subtree, assigns curr list head as root, and builds right subtree in linear O(N).

fields.question_text: 15. In Two Sum IV - Input is a BST (find 2 nodes summing to Target), what space-efficient technique runs in O(N) time and O(H) space?
fields.option_a: Two BST Iterators (1 normal Inorder, 1 Reverse Inorder)
fields.explanation: Two iterators act like two pointers L and R on sorted array, requiring only O(H) stack memory.

fields.question_text: 16. What algorithm restores a BST where EXACTLY TWO nodes were swapped accidentally (Recover BST)?
fields.option_a: Inorder traversal tracking prev node; detect 1st swap (prev > curr) and 2nd swap (prev > curr), then swap back values
fields.explanation: Inorder traversal on BST is strictly sorted. Swapped nodes create 1 or 2 inverted adjacent pairs in O(N) time & O(1) space.

fields.question_text: 17. What is the time complexity to Construct a BST from a Given Preorder Traversal array of size N?
fields.option_a: O(N) passing upper bound constraint down recursive calls
fields.explanation: Using upper bound constraint checks whether next preorder value belongs to current subtree in linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 18. What is the Range Sum of BST (sum of node values in range [Low, High]) time complexity?
fields.option_a: O(N) worst case, pruned branches skip subtrees out of range
fields.explanation: Pruning subtrees where root < Low (skip left) or root > High (skip right) optimizes search traversal.

fields.question_text: 19. What data structure maintains dynamic median of data stream in O(log N) insert time?
fields.option_a: Self-Balancing BST (or Dual Heaps: Max-Heap for left half, Min-Heap for right half)
fields.explanation: Dual heaps or balanced BST keep sizes equalized, yielding stream median in O(1) access and O(log N) insertion.

fields.question_text: 20. In BST Inorder Successor search without parent pointers, what node is tracked when moving LEFT?
fields.option_a: Current node is candidate successor (successor = curr)
fields.explanation: When moving left, current root is larger than target, so it becomes potential candidate successor.

fields.question_text: 21. What is the Largest BST Subtree in Binary Tree algorithm time complexity?
fields.option_a: O(N) bottom-up returning (is_bst, size, min_val, max_val)
fields.explanation: Bottom-up postorder aggregates subtree range bounds and node count, verifying BST status in linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 22. Why does a standard BST fail to guarantee O(log N) operational performance in real-world applications?
fields.option_a: Sorted or semi-sorted insertion sequences cause tree height to degrade to O(N)
fields.explanation: Without self-balancing mechanisms, sequential inserts build skewed line trees of height N.

fields.question_text: 23. In BST insertion, where is a new unique key inserted?
fields.option_a: Always as a NEW LEAF node at appropriate NULL pointer position
fields.explanation: Standard BST insertion traverses down search path until reaching NULL leaf position where node is attached.

fields.question_text: 24. In BST, what is the Inorder Predecessor of a node X with a LEFT child?
fields.option_a: The MAXIMUM key node in X's LEFT subtree (rightmost node of left child)
fields.explanation: Inorder predecessor is the largest value smaller than X, located at rightmost node of left subtree.

fields.question_text: 25. What property distinguishes BST from a Binary Heap?
fields.option_a: BST enforces Left < Root < Right order; Heap enforces Parent >= Child (Max-Heap) across both children
fields.explanation: BST maintains horizontal search ordering; Binary Heap maintains vertical priority parent-child ordering.

fields.question_text: 1. What is an AVL Tree?
fields.option_a: Self-balancing Binary Search Tree where height difference between left and right subtrees of EVERY node is at most 1
fields.explanation: AVL tree is the first self-balancing BST; height balance factor is strictly restricted to {-1, 0, +1}.

fields.question_text: 2. How is the Balance Factor (BF) of a node calculated in an AVL Tree?
fields.explanation: Balance factor equals height of left child minus height of right child.

fields.question_text: 3. What values of Balance Factor indicate that an AVL tree node is OUT OF BALANCE and requires rotation?
fields.option_a: BF > 1 or BF < -1 (i.e. BF = +2 or BF = -2)
fields.explanation: Valid balance factors are -1, 0, +1. Any value outside this range (e.g. +2 or -2) triggers rebalancing rotations.

fields.question_text: 4. What is the MAXIMUM height H of an AVL tree containing N nodes?
fields.explanation: AVL trees strictly guarantee height H < 1.44 log2 N, assuring O(log N) worst-case search time.

fields.question_text: 5. What rotation rebalances a Left-Left (LL) imbalance (node BF = +2, left child BF = +1)?
fields.option_a: Single Right Rotation (Rotate Right around unbalanced node)
fields.explanation: LL imbalance (heavy left-left branch) is resolved by a single Right Rotation.

fields.question_text: 6. What rotation rebalances a Right-Right (RR) imbalance (node BF = -2, right child BF = -1)?
fields.option_a: Single Left Rotation (Rotate Left around unbalanced node)
fields.explanation: RR imbalance (heavy right-right branch) is resolved by a single Left Rotation.

fields.question_text: 7. What rotations rebalance a Left-Right (LR) imbalance (node BF = +2, left child BF = -1)?
fields.option_a: Left Rotation on Left Child, followed by Right Rotation on Unbalanced Node
fields.explanation: LR double rotation first turns left child into LL shape (Left Rotate), then Right Rotates unbalanced root.

fields.question_text: 8. What rotations rebalance a Right-Left (RL) imbalance (node BF = -2, right child BF = +1)?
fields.option_a: Right Rotation on Right Child, followed by Left Rotation on Unbalanced Node
fields.explanation: RL double rotation converts right child to RR shape (Right Rotate), then Left Rotates unbalanced root.

fields.question_text: 9. What is the time complexity of a single tree rotation (Left or Right)?
fields.explanation: Tree rotation only updates 3 pointer references and height numbers, running in constant O(1) time.

fields.question_text: 10. During INSERTION in an AVL tree, what is the maximum number of rotations required to restore balance to the entire tree?
fields.option_a: At most 1 single or 1 double rotation (at most 2 pointer rotations total)
fields.explanation: After inserting a node, rebalancing at the lowest unbalanced ancestor restores height across the whole tree.

fields.question_text: 11. During DELETION in an AVL tree, what is the maximum number of rotations required to restore balance?
fields.option_a: Up to O(log N) rotations (rebalancing may propagate up ancestors to root)
fields.explanation: Node deletion can shorten subtrees, causing height balance fixes to ripple up to log N ancestors.

fields.question_text: 12. What is the worst-case time complexity for Search, Insert, and Delete in an AVL tree of N nodes?
fields.option_a: O(log N) for all three operations
fields.explanation: Strict height balance H = O(log N) guarantees O(log N) worst-case time for search, insert, and delete.

fields.question_text: 13. How does an AVL Tree compare with a Red-Black Tree in terms of search speed vs insertion/deletion overhead?
