fields.option_a: AVL is more strictly balanced (faster searches), but requires more rotations during frequent insertions/deletions
fields.explanation: AVL maintains tighter height bounds (log2 N vs 2 log2 N for Red-Black), yielding faster lookups but higher rebalancing cost.

fields.question_text: 14. What minimum number of nodes N(H) is required to construct an AVL tree of height H?
fields.explanation: Minimal AVL trees (Fibonacci Trees) satisfy N(H) = N(H-1) + N(H-2) + 1 with base cases N(0)=1, N(1)=2.

fields.question_text: 15. In Right Rotation around node Z (with left child Y and Y's right child T2), where does T2 attach after rotation?
fields.option_a: T2 becomes the LEFT child of node Z
fields.option_b: T2 becomes right child of Y
fields.explanation: Right rotation sets Y->right = Z and Z->left = T2, preserving BST order since T2 values lie between Y and Z.

fields.question_text: 16. In Left Rotation around node X (with right child Y and Y's left child T2), where does T2 attach after rotation?
fields.option_a: T2 becomes the RIGHT child of node X
fields.option_b: T2 becomes left child of Y
fields.explanation: Left rotation sets Y->left = X and X->right = T2, preserving BST ordering.

fields.question_text: 17. What extra data field must every node in an AVL tree store?
fields.option_a: Height of the node (or Balance Factor)
fields.explanation: AVL nodes maintain an integer 'height' field to compute balance factor during bottom-up recursion.

fields.question_text: 18. What is the space complexity of storing an AVL tree of N nodes?
fields.option_a: O(N) memory for nodes and height fields
fields.explanation: N nodes with pointers, keys, and integer height fields consume linear O(N) memory.

fields.question_text: 19. If an AVL tree node has height 0 (leaf), what is its height after inserting a single child?
fields.explanation: Height = 1 + max(left_height, right_height). Parent of leaf has height 1.

fields.question_text: 20. What is the height of an empty (NULL) subtree in AVL balance factor calculations?
fields.explanation: NULL subtree height is treated as -1, so a leaf node with two NULL children has height 1 + max(-1, -1) = 0.

fields.question_text: 21. Why are AVL trees preferred over Red-Black trees in lookup-heavy database index applications?
fields.option_a: Stricter balance factor guarantees shorter tree height, minimizing disk read / pointer traversal operations
fields.explanation: Shallow height minimizes comparison steps, making AVL optimal for read-intensive databases.

fields.question_text: 22. In AVL tree rebalancing after insertion, how do you determine whether an imbalance at node Z is LL vs LR?
fields.option_a: Check left child Y: if inserted key < Y.key it is LL; if inserted key > Y.key it is LR
fields.explanation: Key comparison identifies whether inserted node fell into left child's left subtree (LL) or right subtree (LR).

fields.question_text: 23. In an AVL tree with 1 node, what is the tree height (using 0-based root convention)?
fields.explanation: Single root node tree has height 0 under standard edge-count height convention.

fields.question_text: 24. What happens if you attempt to insert a duplicate key into a standard AVL Tree?
fields.option_a: Duplicates are rejected/ignored OR stored in node frequency counter
fields.explanation: Standard BSTs ignore duplicate keys or maintain a frequency count field in existing node.

fields.question_text: 25. Who invented the AVL Tree data structure in 1962?
fields.explanation: AVL tree was invented in 1962 by Soviet mathematicians Georgy Adelson-Velsky and Evgenii Landis.

fields.question_text: 1. What ordering property defines a MAX-HEAP?
fields.option_a: Every parent node key is GREATER than or equal to its children keys (Root is Maximum)
fields.explanation: Max-Heap property enforces parent key >= children keys; max element always resides at root.

fields.question_text: 2. What ordering property defines a MIN-HEAP?
fields.option_a: Every parent node key is LESS than or equal to its children keys (Root is Minimum)
fields.explanation: Min-Heap property enforces parent key <= children keys; min element always resides at root.

fields.question_text: 3. What structural property must every Binary Heap satisfy?
fields.option_a: Must be a Complete Binary Tree (all levels filled except possibly last, filled left-to-right)
fields.explanation: Complete binary tree property allows storing heaps compactly in arrays without empty slot gaps.

fields.question_text: 4. In 0-based array heap representation, given parent index i, what are the left child, right child, and parent indices?
fields.option_c: left = i + 1, right = i + 2, parent = i - 1
fields.option_d: left = i * 2, right = i * 4, parent = i / 4
fields.explanation: 0-based array index arithmetic maps left child = 2i + 1, right child = 2i + 2, parent = (i - 1) // 2.

fields.question_text: 5. What is the time complexity to INSERT a new element into a Binary Heap of N elements?
fields.option_a: O(log N) using Percolate Up / Bubble Up
fields.explanation: Append to array end, then bubble up along tree height O(log N) to restore heap property.

fields.question_text: 6. What is the time complexity to EXTRACT MAX / MIN (pop root) from a Binary Heap of N elements?
fields.option_a: O(log N) using Percolate Down / Heapify
fields.explanation: Swap root with last leaf element, remove last element, and percolate down root in O(log N) time.

fields.question_text: 7. What is the time complexity to BUILD A HEAP (Heapify) from an unsorted array of N elements?
fields.explanation: Bottom-up heapify calling percolate_down from non-leaf nodes N/2 down to 0 sums to O(N) linear time.

fields.question_text: 8. What is the worst-case time complexity of HEAP SORT on an array of N elements?
fields.option_a: O(N log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space
fields.explanation: Build Max-Heap O(N), then repeatedly extract max and swap with end N times (N * log N = O(N log N) in-place).

fields.question_text: 9. Is Heap Sort a STABLE sorting algorithm?
fields.option_a: No, non-adjacent element swaps break relative order of equal keys
fields.explanation: Heap sift-down swaps distant elements, making Heap Sort unstable.

fields.question_text: 10. In array of size N representing Max-Heap, at what index do LEAF nodes start (0-based indexing)?
fields.explanation: Nodes from floor(N/2) to N-1 are leaf nodes with no children, requiring no heapify.

fields.question_text: 11. What is the time complexity to find the MINIMUM element in a MAX-HEAP of N elements?
fields.option_a: O(N) search among leaf nodes floor(N/2)..N-1
fields.explanation: In Max-Heap, minimum element can be any leaf node; searching N/2 leaves takes linear O(N) time.

fields.question_text: 12. In K-th Largest Element in an Array problem, what heap size should be maintained to achieve O(N log K) time?
fields.option_a: Min-Heap of size K (root holds K-th largest element)
fields.explanation: Maintaining size-K Min-Heap evicts smaller elements, leaving K largest elements with minimum at root.

fields.question_text: 13. In Find Median from Data Stream, what two heaps are used?
fields.option_a: Max-Heap for lower half of numbers, Min-Heap for upper half of numbers
fields.explanation: Max-Heap (lower half) top and Min-Heap (upper half) top yield median in O(1) time.

fields.question_text: 14. What is the time complexity of Merging K Sorted Lists of total N elements using Min-Heap?
fields.explanation: Min-heap holds first element from each of K lists; extracting min and pushing next element takes O(N log K).

fields.question_text: 15. What is a 'd-ary Heap'?
fields.option_a: Heap where each non-leaf node has d children instead of 2
fields.explanation: d-ary heap increases fan-out: decrease-key runs faster O(log_d N), while extract-min takes O(d log_d N).

fields.question_text: 16. In Fibonacci Heap, what is the amortized time complexity of Insert, Find-Min, and Decrease-Key operations?
fields.option_a: O(1) amortized time for Insert, Find-Min, and Decrease-Key
fields.explanation: Fibonacci Heap achieves O(1) amortized for insert, find-min, decrease-key (Extract-Min remains O(log N)).

fields.question_text: 17. What graph shortest path algorithm benefits directly from Fibonacci Heap's O(1) Decrease-Key performance?
fields.option_a: Dijkstra's Algorithm (improves time from O(E log V) to O(E + V log V))
fields.explanation: O(1) decrease-key lowers edge relaxations cost to O(E), improving total time to O(E + V log V).

fields.question_text: 18. What heap operation is used in Priority Queue to change an element's value and fix heap order?
fields.option_a: Decrease-Key / Increase-Key (percolate up if smaller in Min-Heap, down if larger)
fields.explanation: Updating value and calling bubble-up or sift-down restores heap property in O(log N) time.

fields.question_text: 19. In Top K Frequent Elements problem (array of N numbers), how can you solve it in O(N log K) time?
fields.option_a: Count frequencies using Hash Map, then maintain Min-Heap of size K based on frequency
fields.explanation: Min-Heap of size K retains K highest frequency entries, taking O(N log K) overall time.

fields.question_text: 20. How do you implement a Max-Heap in Python's heapq module (which only provides Min-Heap by default)?
fields.option_a: Multiply numerical values by -1 before push and after pop
fields.explanation: Negating numbers flips inequality sign, allowing heapq min-heap to function as max-heap.

fields.question_text: 21. What is the space complexity of storing a Binary Heap of N elements in an array?
fields.explanation: Binary heap uses array buffer of size N without extra pointer overhead.

fields.question_text: 22. In Reorganize String problem (rearrange so no adjacent identical chars), what heap strategy is used?
fields.option_a: Max-Heap of character frequencies; pop top 2 most frequent characters per step
fields.explanation: Popping top 2 distinct characters guarantees adjacent characters differ while exhausting high frequencies.

fields.question_text: 23. What is the time complexity to Peek the Root element of a Min-Heap?
fields.explanation: Root element resides at array index 0; peeking accesses heap[0] in constant O(1) time.

fields.question_text: 24. In Minimum Cost to Connect Ropes problem, what heap strategy minimizes total cost?
fields.option_a: Min-Heap: repeatedly pop 2 smallest ropes, add sum to cost, push sum back to Min-Heap
fields.explanation: Greedy choice combining two shortest ropes at each step minimizes accumulated connection cost (Huffman coding).

fields.question_text: 25. Which heap type supports O(1) Meld (merge two heaps) operation?
fields.option_a: Pairing Heap / Fibonacci Heap / Binomial Heap
fields.explanation: Mergeable heaps (Binomial, Fibonacci, Pairing) support uniting two heaps efficiently.

fields.question_text: 1. What is the space complexity of storing a Graph G(V, E) using an Adjacency Matrix vs Adjacency List?
fields.option_a: Adjacency Matrix: O(V^2); Adjacency List: O(V + E)
fields.explanation: Adjacency matrix allocates V x V grid O(V^2); Adjacency list stores only actual edges O(V + E).

fields.question_text: 2. What graph traversal algorithm uses a FIFO Queue and finds Shortest Path in UNWEIGHTED graphs?
fields.explanation: BFS explores graph level-by-level, guaranteeing shortest path in unweighted graphs in O(V + E) time.

fields.question_text: 3. What graph traversal uses a Call Stack / Recursion and explores deep along edges before backtracking?
fields.explanation: DFS traverses deeply down path branches until hitting dead ends, then backtracks.

fields.question_text: 4. What is the time complexity of BFS and DFS traversals on a graph represented as an Adjacency List?
fields.explanation: Every vertex and edge is visited a constant number of times, yielding linear O(V + E) complexity.

fields.question_text: 5. How do you detect a Cycle in an UNDIRECTED Graph using Disjoint Set Union (DSU)?
fields.option_a: If find(u) == find(v) for edge (u, v), a cycle exists
fields.explanation: If two endpoints of an edge already belong to the same connected component set, adding the edge forms a cycle.

fields.question_text: 6. How do you detect a Cycle in a DIRECTED Graph using DFS?
fields.option_a: Track visit states: Unvisited (0), Visiting/Active in Call Stack (1), Visited (2). Encountering state 1 indicates back-edge cycle
fields.explanation: Re-encountering a node currently in active recursion stack (state 1) identifies a directed back-edge cycle.

fields.question_text: 7. What is Topological Sort?
fields.option_a: Linear ordering of vertices in a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) such that for every directed edge u -> v, u comes before v
fields.explanation: Topological sort orders DAG dependencies (e.g. course prerequisites) in linear O(V + E) time.

fields.question_text: 8. What algorithm uses In-Degree counting and a Queue to perform Topological Sort (Kahn's Algorithm)?
fields.option_a: Kahn's Algorithm: enqueue 0-indegree nodes, pop node, decrement neighbor indegrees, enqueue new 0-indegree nodes
fields.explanation: Kahn's algorithm processes 0-indegree nodes sequentially. If processed nodes < V, graph has a cycle.

fields.question_text: 9. What shortest path algorithm finds single-source shortest paths in NON-NEGATIVE weighted graphs using Min-Priority Queue?
fields.explanation: Greedy choice using Min-PQ relaxes shortest distance estimates in O((V + E) log V) time.

fields.question_text: 10. Why does Dijkstra's Algorithm FAIL or enter infinite loops on graphs with NEGATIVE edge weights?
fields.option_a: Greedy assumption breaks (visited distance can be re-shortened by negative edge), causing incorrect distances or infinite loops in negative cycles
fields.explanation: Dijkstra assumes distance estimates never decrease once popped. Negative edges violate this greedy principle.

fields.question_text: 11. What algorithm computes single-source shortest paths on graphs with NEGATIVE edge weights and detects negative weight cycles?
fields.explanation: Bellman-Ford relaxes all E edges V-1 times. A 16th relaxation loop detecting distance decreases confirms a negative cycle.

fields.question_text: 12. What is the time complexity of Bellman-Ford Algorithm on graph G(V, E)?
fields.explanation: V-1 iterations scanning all E edges yields O(V * E) time complexity.

fields.question_text: 13. What algorithm computes ALL-PAIRS shortest paths between every pair of vertices in O(V^3) time?
fields.explanation: Dynamic programming matrix update dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]) across 3 nested loops V times.

fields.question_text: 14. What is a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST)?
fields.option_a: Subset of edges connecting all V vertices in a weighted connected graph without cycles, with MINIMUM total edge weight
fields.explanation: MST spans all V vertices using V-1 edges with smallest cumulative weight sum.

fields.question_text: 15. How does Kruskal's Algorithm build a Minimum Spanning Tree?
fields.option_a: Sort all E edges by weight, iterate sorted edges, add edge to MST if DSU find(u) != find(v)
fields.option_b: Grow tree from single root using PQ
fields.explanation: Greedy edge choice combined with Disjoint Set Union (DSU) cycle prevention runs in O(E log E) time.

fields.question_text: 16. How does Prim's Algorithm build a Minimum Spanning Tree?
fields.option_a: Start from arbitrary vertex, maintain Min-PQ of edges connected to visited tree, greedily pick smallest edge to unvisited node
fields.explanation: Prim's grows a single connected component tree out from start vertex in O(E log V) time.

fields.question_text: 17. What is a Bipartite Graph?
fields.option_a: Graph whose vertices can be divided into 2 disjoint sets U and V such that every edge connects a vertex in U to a vertex in V
fields.explanation: Graph is bipartite if and only if it contains NO odd-length cycles (validated via 2-coloring BFS/DFS).

fields.question_text: 18. What is a Strongly Connected Component (SCC) in a Directed Graph?
fields.option_a: Maximal subgraph where EVERY vertex is reachable from every other vertex in the subgraph
fields.explanation: SCC represents maximal vertex sets with mutual reachability u -> v and v -> u.

fields.question_text: 19. What algorithm finds all Strongly Connected Components in a Directed Graph in linear O(V + E) time using low-link values?
fields.explanation: Tarjan's algorithm uses DFS discovery times and low-link values on a stack to extract SCCs in O(V + E).

fields.question_text: 20. What is an Articulation Point (Cut Vertex) in a graph?
fields.option_a: A vertex whose removal increases the number of connected components (disconnects the graph)
fields.explanation: Cut vertices are critical nodes whose failure fractures the graph network into isolated sub-graphs.

fields.question_text: 21. What condition identifies a Bridge (Cut Edge) in graph DFS low-link calculation for edge u -> v?
fields.explanation: If lowest discovery time reachable from v is strictly greater than u's discovery time, edge (u, v) is a Bridge.

fields.question_text: 22. In Network Flow, what theorem states that Maximum Flow through a network equals Minimum Capacity Cut?
fields.explanation: Max-Flow Min-Cut theorem establishes duality between maximum flow and minimum bottleneck cut capacity.

fields.question_text: 23. What is an Eulerian Path in a graph?
fields.option_a: Path that visits EVERY EDGE in the graph exactly once
fields.explanation: Eulerian path traverses every edge once. Exists if connected graph has 0 or 2 vertices of odd degree.

fields.question_text: 24. What is a Hamiltonian Path in a graph?
fields.option_a: Path that visits EVERY VERTEX in the graph exactly once
fields.explanation: Hamiltonian path visits every vertex once (NP-complete problem solved via backtracking / Bitmask DP).

fields.question_text: 25. What is the Handshaking Lemma for undirected graphs?
fields.option_a: Sum of degrees of all vertices equals 2 * |E|
fields.explanation: Because every undirected edge contributes 1 to the degree of two endpoints, total degree sum = 2 * |E|.

fields.question_text: 1. What TWO core properties must a problem satisfy to be solvable using Dynamic Programming?
fields.explanation: DP applies when optimal solution is built from optimal subproblems AND identical subproblems recur multiple times.

fields.question_text: 2. What is Top-Down Dynamic Programming?
fields.option_a: Recursion combined with Memoization table/hash map to cache calculated state results
fields.explanation: Top-down starts from original problem target and recurses downwards, caching subproblem solutions.

fields.question_text: 3. What is Bottom-Up Dynamic Programming?
fields.option_a: Iterative Tabulation filling DP table starting from Base Cases up to Target state
fields.explanation: Bottom-up solves smallest subproblems first, building state transitions iteratively without call stack.

fields.question_text: 4. What is the time & space complexity of calculating N-th Fibonacci number using DP Tabulation with 2 variables?
fields.option_a: O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space
fields.explanation: Maintaining prev1 and prev2 updates fibonacci state in linear O(N) time and constant O(1) space.

fields.question_text: 5. In 0/1 Knapsack Problem (N items, Weight W), what choices are available for each item?
fields.option_a: Include item at most ONCE or Exclude item
fields.explanation: 0/1 Knapsack restricts each item to 0 (exclude) or 1 (include) decision.

fields.question_text: 6. What is the time and space complexity of standard 2D DP for 0/1 Knapsack (N items, capacity W)?
fields.option_a: O(N * W) time and O(N * W) space (reducible to O(W) space)
fields.explanation: DP table of size (N+1) x (W+1) fills each entry in O(1) time. Space compresses to 1D array O(W).

fields.question_text: 7. How does Unbounded Knapsack differ from 0/1 Knapsack?
fields.option_a: Items can be chosen and reused an INFINITE number of times
fields.explanation: Unbounded knapsack allows unlimited copies of each item (e.g. Coin Change problem).

fields.question_text: 8. What state transition equation defines Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) for S1[i-1] == S2[j-1]?
fields.explanation: Matching characters extend previous diagonal common subsequence dp[i-1][j-1] by 1.

fields.question_text: 9. What state transition equation defines LCS when S1[i-1] != S2[j-1]?
fields.explanation: Non-matching characters take maximum of skipping char from S1 vs skipping char from S2.

fields.question_text: 10. In Coin Change Problem (minimum coins to make amount A), what is the state transition for dp[i]?
fields.option_a: dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - coin]) for all coins <= i
fields.explanation: Taking coin adds 1 coin to subproblem dp[i - coin], minimizing across all valid coin choices.

fields.question_text: 11. In Coin Change 2 Problem (total UNIQUE COMBINATIONS to make amount A), what is the loop order?
fields.option_a: Outer loop over coins, inner loop over amounts from coin to A
fields.option_b: Outer loop over amounts, inner loop over coins
fields.explanation: Outer coin loop ensures coins are considered in fixed order, counting combinations (unordered) rather than permutations.

fields.question_text: 12. What is the time complexity to find Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) of length N using DP + Binary Search (Patience Sorting)?
fields.explanation: Maintaining tail array and using std::lower_bound binary search runs in O(N log N) time & O(N) space.

fields.question_text: 13. In Edit Distance (Levenshtein) between S1 (len M) and S2 (len N), what is the transition when S1[i-1] != S2[j-1]?
fields.option_a: dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]) (Delete, Insert, Replace)
fields.explanation: Min cost takes 1 + minimum of Delete dp[i-1][j], Insert dp[i][j-1], or Replace dp[i-1][j-1].

fields.question_text: 14. In Partition Equal Subset Sum (can array sum S be split into 2 equal halves S/2), what DP variant does this reduce to?
fields.option_a: 0/1 Knapsack Subset Sum with target capacity = TotalSum / 2
fields.explanation: If TotalSum is even, check if subset exists with sum equal to TotalSum / 2 using 0/1 Knapsack.

fields.question_text: 15. In Matrix Chain Multiplication (find min scalar multiplications to multiply N matrices), what DP pattern is used?
fields.option_a: Interval / Range Dynamic Programming dp[i][j] for subsegment range [i..j]
fields.explanation: Interval DP evaluates splitting range [i..j] at partition k (i <= k < j), minimizing dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + cost.

fields.question_text: 16. What is the time complexity of Matrix Chain Multiplication for N matrices using Interval DP?
fields.explanation: Length loop O(N), start loop O(N), and split point k loop O(N) multiply to O(N^3) total operations.

fields.question_text: 17. What is Bitmask Dynamic Programming?
fields.option_a: Using integer bitmask (e.g. 0 to 2^N - 1) to represent subset state of visited elements in NP-hard problems
fields.explanation: Bitmasks represent subset combinations as binary integers, optimizing state space for N <= 20.

fields.question_text: 18. What is the time complexity of Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) using Bitmask DP (Held-Karp Algorithm) for N cities?
fields.option_a: O(N^2 * 2^N) time, reduced from brute force O(N!)
fields.explanation: State dp(mask, u) has 2^N * N states; transitioning across N neighbors takes O(N^2 * 2^N) time.

fields.question_text: 19. In Palindromic Partitioning II (min cuts to partition string into palindromes), what is optimal time complexity?
fields.option_a: O(N^2) by precomputing palindrome matrix then 1D DP min cut
fields.explanation: Expand around center precomputes palindrome table in O(N^2); 1D DP calculates min cuts in O(N^2).

fields.question_text: 20. In House Robber II (houses arranged in a CIRCLE), how is circular constraint handled?
fields.option_a: Run 1D DP twice: once for range [0..N-2] (skip last), once for range [1..N-1] (skip first), take max
fields.explanation: Because house 0 and house N-1 cannot both be robbed, running 1D DP on both linear subranges solves problem.

fields.question_text: 21. What optimization technique reduces DP transitions from O(N) to O(1) in convex DP recurrence functions?
fields.option_a: Convex Hull Trick (CHT) / Monotonic Queue Optimization
fields.explanation: Convex Hull Trick maintains linear convex functions envelope, reducing DP state transitions to O(1) or O(log N).

fields.question_text: 22. In N-th Fibonacci number using Matrix Exponentiation, what is the time complexity?
fields.option_a: O(log N) using binary matrix power
fields.explanation: Raising transition matrix [[1,1],[1,0]] to power N using binary exponentiation takes O(log N) time.

fields.question_text: 23. In Word Break Problem (dict of words, check if S can be segmented), what is time complexity using 1D DP?
fields.option_a: O(N^2 * L) where N is len(S) and L is max word len in dict
fields.explanation: dp[i] is true if dp[j] is true AND S[j..i] exists in dictionary set for j < i.

fields.question_text: 24. In Wildcard Matching ('?' matches 1 char, '*' matches any sequence), what is 2D DP matrix transition for '*'?
fields.option_a: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] (match 1+ chars) OR dp[i][j-1] (match empty sequence)
fields.explanation: '*' can either absorb current text character dp[i-1][j] or act as empty string dp[i][j-1].

fields.question_text: 25. Why is Space Optimization possible in many 2D DP problems (e.g. 0/1 Knapsack, Unique Paths)?
fields.option_a: State dp[i][j] depends ONLY on previous row dp[i-1], allowing rolling array of 1 or 2 rows
fields.explanation: When transition only references row i-1, keeping 1D rolling array reduces auxiliary space from O(R*C) to O(C).
